title: problem-management output
description: Structured output: an ITIL Problem Management record produced by the problem-management skill. Adapted from @windyroad/itil (MIT).

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the problem.

problem_statement.description: One-sentence statement of the symptom (not a guessed cause).

proactive.description: True if discovered proactively (latent defect) with no triggering incident.

linked_incidents.description: IDs or references of incidents this problem caused. May be empty only when proactive is true.

owner.description: Person or team owning the investigation/fix.

root_cause.description: The confirmed, evidence-backed root cause. Required to enter known-error.

summary.description: Plain-language statement of the confirmed root cause.

analysis_method.description: Technique used to reach the root cause.

evidence.description: Evidence supporting the root cause: log lines, commit SHAs, metrics, reproduction steps.

confirmed.description: True once the cause is proven (e.g. reproduction), not merely hypothesized.

workaround.description: Documented mitigation on-call applies to the incident while the permanent fix is pending. Required to enter known-error.

wsjf.description: Weighted Shortest Job First scoring. score = cost_of_delay / job_size.

cost_of_delay.description: Value lost by leaving the problem unfixed; derived from impact x likelihood (severity).

job_size.description: Relative effort to ship the permanent fix (e.g. XS=1..XL=8).

resolution.description: How the problem was permanently resolved.

fix_description.description: What was changed to remove the root cause (not the workaround).

released_in.description: Version, commit, or deploy where the fix shipped.

verified.description: True once the fix is confirmed to resolve the problem. Required to close.

verification_evidence.description: Evidence the fix worked: passing reproduction test, clean metrics window, user confirmation.

parked_reason.description: Documented reason when status is parked (e.g. upstream-blocked, out-of-appetite, deferred).
